title: Upcoming IPOs, Explained Simply — July 2026
description: Learn about IC Electricals Company Limited's upcoming SME IPO. Understand what an Initial Public Offering (IPO) is and why companies do them.

faq.q: How do I even apply for an IPO?
faq.a: You can apply for an IPO through your bank's net banking portal using the ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount) facility, or through your stockbroker's online platform.
The lot size is the minimum number of shares you must bid for in an IPO. You cannot apply for fewer than the specified lot size.
An IPO is oversubscribed when the total demand for shares (the number of applications received) is more than the number of shares the company is offering.

faq.q: What is the difference between a mainboard IPO and an SME IPO?
faq.a: Mainboard IPOs are typically for larger companies and list on the main platforms of NSE and BSE. SME IPOs are for Small and Medium Enterprises and list on dedicated SME platforms (like NSE Emerge or BSE SME).

ASBA stands for Application Supported by Blocked Amount. When you apply for an IPO using ASBA, the application money is blocked in your bank account but not debited until shares are allotted to you. If you don't receive an allotment, the money is simply unblocked.
